records.label: Patient 1
quotes: We report two unrelated patients with this disease who have survived into early childhood with mild cutaneous involvement, in whom we have identified pathogenetic mutations in ITGB4.
The first patient was a compound heterozygote for a splice site mutation in exon 30 (3793 + 1G-to-A) and a non-sense mutation in exon 36 (W1478X)

records.label: Patient 2
quotes: the second was a compound heterozygote for a missense mutation in exon 3 (C38R) and a 1 bp deletion in exon 36 (4776delG)
We report two unrelated patients with this disease who have survived into early childhood with mild cutaneous involvement

records.label: 49-year-old female patient

phenotypes.text: mild blistering of hands and feet
intraepidermal blister cleavage low in basal keratinocytes through hemidesmosome attachment plaque

quotes: The patient, a 49-y-old female, had mild blistering of hands and feet from birth on, dystrophy of the nails with onychogryposis, and enamel hypoplasia. She had no alopecia and no history of pyloric atresia.

The 4733delCT mutation was heterozygously present in the DNA. The patient is also expected to be heterozygous for a null allele, as no full-size protein was detected in vitro and the epitope 450-11 A was absent in vivo.

notes.statement: In a consensus expert review, Has et al. (2020) reclassified inherited epidermolysis bullosa (EB) and other disorders with skin fragility using new clinical and molecular data. They introduced the concept of genetic disorders with skin fragility, with classical EB as the prototype.
quotes: We sought to reclassify disorders with skin fragility, with a focus on EB, based on new clinical and molecular data.
In this latest consensus report, we introduce the concept of genetic disorders with skin fragility, of which classical EB represents the prototype.

notes.statement: Jonkman et al. (2002) found that a 2-bp deletion (4733delCT) in ITGB4 resulted in in-frame skipping of exon 36 and a deduced 50-amino acid deletion (residues 1450-1499) within the third fibronectin type III repeat of the beta-4 cytoplasmic domain; immunoblot showed a 5-kDa shorter beta-4 polypeptide. The patient was expected to also carry a null allele, as no full-size protein was detected.
quotes: At the molecular level the phenotype was caused by a novel 2 bp deletion 4733delCT in ITGB4, resulting in in-frame skipping of exon 36 and a deduced 50 amino acid deletion (1450-1499) within the third fibronectin type III repeat in the cytoplasmic domain of the integrin beta4 polypeptide.
Immunoblot analysis demonstrated a 5 kDa shorter beta4 polypeptide.

notes.statement: Jonkman et al. (2002) concluded that deletion of the third fibronectin type III repeat of the integrin beta-4 cytoplasmic domain, thought to interact with BP180/type XVII collagen, is pathogenic and results in a mild phenotype with predominant features of epidermolysis bullosa simplex. Immunofluorescence showed absent binding of antibody 450-11A against this repeat and reduced binding of antibodies to the amino- and carboxy-terminal ends.
quotes: Immuno-fluorescence microscopy revealed absent binding of monoclonal antibody 450-11 A against the third fibronectin III repeat on the intracellular domain of integrin beta4, whereas binding was reduced with monoclonal antibodies recognizing epitopes on amino-terminal and carboxy-terminal ends of the polypeptide.

These data show that deletion of the third fibronectin type III repeat in the cytoplasmic domain of integrin beta4, which is thought to interact with BP180/type XVII collagen, is clinically pathogenic and results in a mild phenotype with predominant features of epidermolysis bullosa simplex.

notes.statement: Inoue et al. (2000) reported a homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D, that they proposed disrupts hemidesmosome assembly and underlies non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia.
quotes: A homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D, that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly

notes.statement: Mellerio et al. (1998) suggested that although the nonsense and deletion mutations in ITGB4 were predicted to markedly reduce beta-4 integrin mRNA levels, the missense or splice site mutation on the second allele may allow synthesis of some functional, albeit perturbed, beta-4 polypeptide, possibly explaining the mild phenotype and survival of their 2 patients.
quotes: Although the non-sense and deletion mutations are predicted to result in markedly reduced beta4 integrin mRNA levels, the presence of the missense or splice site mutation on the second allele may enable the synthesis of some functional, albeit perturbed, beta4 polypeptide.

notes.statement: Pulkkinen et al. (1998) found novel ITGB4 mutations on 5 alleles in 3 patients with the lethal form of epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia. Three of the 4 distinct mutations were predicted to truncate the polypeptide. The authors suggested that the missense mutation in the extracellular domain of beta-4 integrin may affect ligand binding or dimerization of the alpha-6 and beta-4 subunits.
quotes: Thus, three of four distinct mutations predicted truncated polypeptide chains, whereas the missense mutation in the extracellular domain of beta4 integrin may affect ligand binding or dimerization of alpha6 and beta4 integrin subunits.

notes.statement: Pulkkinen et al. (1998) described epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia as a clinically and genetically heterogeneous autosomal recessive blistering disorder with lethal and nonlethal variants.
quotes: Epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia (EB-PA; OMIM 226730) is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous autosomal recessive blistering disorder, including lethal and nonlethal variants.
